quote: as 345 Burning Bridge Road in Ojo Aniso, New Mexico. Is that correct?
stewart_read: The rep's address record is wrong (customer corrects both the city and the community name), and the rep then spends roughly 40 seconds (00:41-01:44) trying to relocate the address on a map while the customer waits silently. This is rep-side time-burn on a basic verify step, not customer resistance.
coaching_implication: Coach on pre-call data prep and faster recovery when the on-file address is wrong -- confirm verbally and move on rather than stalling live on a map lookup.

quote: Well, I do have a solar, that runs, the reason why I wanted was asking because I have a solar, and when the solar was brought to me, the solar on it says, Sacred Power.
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing solar system from a named company (Sacred Power) as part of explaining her ask. The rep never runs any orphaned_flow questions (own vs. lease, system working, panel size) before reaching the DQ decision seconds later.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep missed a required qualification step. Strategic read considered and rejected -- there is no evidence the rep intentionally skipped orphaned_flow to save time; the pivot to refrigerator-specific language at 03:42 suggests the rep simply locked onto the appliance request without registering the system-ownership disclosure.
coaching_implication: Even in calls that end in DQ, the orphaned_flow questions should be asked for the record and for potential future routing (e.g., system health, buyout status) -- takes 15-20 seconds and creates a clean data trail.

quote: Okay. We actually don't have solar refrigerators here, so I I do apologize.
stewart_read: The customer's ask, stated plainly at 03:39 ('I was looking for a refrigerator for for a solar'), is for a specific appliance Ion does not sell. The rep identifies this correctly and quickly. This is not a missed solar-service opportunity -- it is an accurate, fast disqualification on a genuine product mismatch.
alternative_hypothesis: Alternative considered: rep should have explored the existing Sacred Power system for a possible service/replacement lead. Rejected as the primary read because the customer's own words narrow the ask to an appliance, not a system evaluation -- the DQ is very likely correct regardless of whether orphaned_flow was run.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed on the DQ decision itself; the gap is procedural (see the prior_contact_probe_miss entry above), not judgment.

quote: I'll give you off our list, though, but you have a good rest of your day.
stewart_read: The call ends with a list-removal offer and a pleasantry but no structured close -- no recap of why she was disqualified, no note of what she should do if her needs change. The schema has no defined DQ-close protocol, so this is a gap in coverage rather than a violation of an existing rule.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: Ion's schema has no defined 'clean DQ close' template. Until one exists, coach reps to at least state plainly why the request doesn't fit (appliance vs. service) so the customer has clarity, not just a polite goodbye.
